data.narrative:
New Limit, a Series C biotech company founded by Armstrong, Byers, and Kimmel, is valued at $3.1B post-money following $610M+ in cumulative fundraising. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 11 comparable companies: 3 public-market peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $3.1B base, yielding $5.3B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and Eikon Therapeutics ($539M)—produces a median of $3.8B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 6.6x across the three public tickers) cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures, standard for private companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $3.2B to $6.1B, with a median of $4.5B. New Limit's current $3.1B valuation sits near the lower bound, reflecting its Series C stage. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory, pipeline maturity, and capital efficiency—data not provided here. The wide dispersion in peer valuations ($539M–$10.3B) underscores sector-specific risk factors and stage heterogeneity within the biotech universe.
